                    ### Question
                    During a study on the immune system, an investigator isolates and labels T cells from the cortex of the thymus. The T cells that do not bind cortical epithelial cells expressing MHC molecules undergo apoptosis within 3–4 days. Which of the following best describes the T cells during this phase of differentiation?

                    ### Options

opb. Th2
opc. CD8+
opd. T cell precursor
ope. CD4+

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
During T cell differentiation in the thymus, T cells undergo positive selection in the cortex, where they interact with MHC molecules presented by cortical epithelial cells. T cells that do not successfully bind to these MHC molecules undergo apoptosis within 3-4 days. This process primarily leads to the differentiation of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, as both subsets are present during this phase. The reasoning chains correctly highlight that CD4+ and CD8+ T cells are the result of this selection process, confirming that the T cells in question are indeed CD4+ and CD8+. The evidence paths regarding the interaction of T lymphocytes with MHC molecules further support this understanding, emphasizing the critical role of MHC in T cell selection. Therefore, the best description of the T cells during this phase of differentiation is that they are both CD4+ and CD8+.
